statement: Households in Kathmandu wait days for private water tankers with no idea of queue position, price or arrival time.
solution: Water Tanker Booking and Queue Tracker
topics: Process scheduling;Semaphores and critical sections;Multithreading;Stored procedures and functions
twist: Treat each tanker as a CPU and each booking as a process: shortest-job-first with aging decides the queue, and a semaphore stops two households claiming the same tanker slot.

statement: During monsoon, villagers learn about landslide-blocked roads only after travelling to the spot.
affected: Commuters and bus drivers in hill districts
topics: Probability distributions;Hypothesis testing;Triggers
twist: Trust a report only when enough independent people agree: a binomial test on the report count decides whether a road is marked blocked, and a trigger expires the mark after six hours.

statement: After an earthquake, relief teams cannot see which wards have already received tents and food.
topics: Transactions and ACID;Locking and deadlock in databases;Stored procedures and functions;Swing GUI
twist: Two wards must never hand out the same tent stock: wrap every handover in a transaction with row locks, and show what happens when two clerks click at the same moment.

statement: Air quality in the valley spikes in winter but schools decide outdoor activities without local readings.
solution: Low-Cost Air Quality Monitor for Schools
topics: Interrupts and DMA;Descriptive statistics;Charts and graphs;Real-time systems
twist: Sensor readings arrive as interrupts, a moving median removes the spikes, and a histogram of the week shows when outdoor play is safe.

statement: River-side settlements get flood warnings too late because gauge readings are not shared locally.
topics: Real-time systems;Socket programming;Descriptive statistics
twist: A river gauge is a hard real-time source: gauges push readings over UDP, and the board raises the alarm when the rise rate passes two standard deviations.

statement: Waste pickers and recyclers have no way to know which households have sorted dry waste ready.
topics: Disk scheduling;Process scheduling;Collections framework;Charts and graphs
twist: Order pickups the way a disk head serves requests: SCAN sweeps the ward once instead of zig-zagging, and a chart shows the distance saved against first-come-first-served.

statement: Farmers sell vegetables to middlemen without knowing that day's Kalimati wholesale price.
solution: Kalimati Price Watch and Sell Planner
topics: Correlation and regression;Descriptive statistics;Charts and graphs;File IO and serialization
twist: Fit a least-squares trend to the last 30 days of prices and tell the farmer whether to sell today or wait, with the correlation coefficient shown as the confidence.

statement: Livestock farmers miss vaccination dates for their animals because records are kept in memory.
topics: Triggers;Stored procedures and functions;Multithreading
twist: A stored procedure works out due dates from each animal's last dose and a trigger queues the SMS the day before, so the schedule lives in the database and not in the app.

statement: Farmers cannot tell which fertilizer their soil needs and overuse urea.
topics: Hypothesis testing;Descriptive statistics;Probability distributions;SQL views
twist: Compare a field's nitrogen reading with the district mean using a one-sample t-test, and advise fertilizer only when the difference is significant.

statement: Cold storage space in districts is booked by phone and often double-booked during harvest.
topics: Memory allocation;Locking and deadlock in databases;Transactions and ACID
twist: Cold-room space is memory: allocate pallets with best-fit, merge freed gaps and show the fragmentation, while a row lock prevents a double booking.

statement: Crop disease spreads because farmers cannot reach an agriculture technician quickly.
topics: Socket programming;Multithreading;File IO and serialization;Query processing and indexing
twist: A TCP server answers many farmers at once with one thread each, stores photos on disk and indexes past answers so a repeat problem gets an instant reply.

statement: Rural health posts run out of essential medicines before the district store even knows.
topics: RMI and distributed objects;Triggers;Backup and recovery;Distributed systems
twist: Each health post keeps its own database and syncs with the district store through RMI, a trigger raises the low-stock alert, and a restore drill proves a post recovers from a power cut.

statement: Parents lose track of their child's vaccination card and miss scheduled doses.
topics: Stored procedures and functions;Triggers;Backup and recovery
twist: Due dates come from a stored function over the national schedule, and a trigger writes an audit row for every dose, so a lost card can be rebuilt from the log.

statement: Ambulance drivers and families waste time finding which hospital has a free ICU bed.
topics: Transactions and ACID;Locking and deadlock in databases;Socket programming;Real-time systems
twist: A wrong bed count can cost a life: serializable transactions make sure two ambulances never get the same last bed, and changes reach every screen over TCP within a second.

statement: Elderly people living alone forget to take daily medicines on time.
affected: Elderly people and their children abroad
solution: Medicine Intake Reminder with Family Alerts
topics: Process scheduling;Real-time systems;Multithreading;Collections framework
twist: A scheduler thread fires reminders in earliest-deadline-first order, and if a dose is not confirmed within 30 minutes the family is alerted.

statement: Female community health volunteers still record household visits on paper registers.
topics: Swing GUI;File IO and serialization;Transactions and ACID;Backup and recovery
twist: Works offline on the volunteer's laptop: Swing forms save to a serialized file, and a sync step replays the changes into MySQL as one transaction.

statement: Students repeat past project ideas because no one checks them against old projects early.
topics: Query processing and indexing;Collections framework;Descriptive statistics
twist: An inverted index and rare-term weights are the database-indexing and information-content ideas from class, applied to the duplicate check itself.

statement: Practical exam marks from lab teachers are typed again by the exam section, causing errors.
solution: Lab Marks Direct Entry and Verification
topics: Database security and access control;Triggers;Transactions and ACID;Swing GUI
twist: Every mark change is written to an audit table by a trigger with a hash of the old value, so a disputed result can be traced to who changed it and when.

statement: Community school teachers have no simple tool to spot students at risk of dropping out.
topics: Chi-square test;Correlation and regression;Charts and graphs
twist: Test whether low attendance and dropping out are really linked using a chi-square test of independence on last year's records, then flag students whose pattern matches.

statement: Students cannot find which senior already solved a lab assignment topic to ask for guidance.
topics: SQL views;Query processing and indexing;Collections framework
twist: Match juniors to seniors with a ranked SQL view over subjects and marks, and show the query plan before and after adding an index.

statement: Homestays in villages are invisible online, so tourists only book city hotels.
topics: Transactions and ACID;Page replacement;Cache and memory hierarchy;Collections framework
twist: Booking runs inside transactions, and the popular listings sit in an LRU cache that you can show beating FIFO on real search logs.

statement: Trekkers on remote trails cannot tell family where they are when there is no internet.
topics: Socket programming;Probability distributions;Multithreading
twist: An SMS link loses messages like an unreliable network: build the check-in protocol with acknowledgements and retries over UDP and measure the loss with a Poisson model.

statement: Tourists are overcharged by taxis because they do not know fair fares between points.
topics: Correlation and regression;Descriptive statistics;Hypothesis testing;Charts and graphs
twist: Fit fare against distance from reported fares, draw the confidence band, and flag any quote more than two standard deviations above it.

statement: Cooperative members cannot see their savings statement without visiting the office.
topics: Database security and access control;SQL views;Stored procedures and functions
twist: Each member sees only their own rows through a view and a role, and the statement comes from a stored procedure: the access-control unit put to work.

statement: Small shopkeepers lend on credit (udharo) and lose track of who owes how much.
topics: Computer arithmetic;Triggers;Transactions and ACID
twist: Money must add up to the last paisa: store amounts as integers, show why floating point drifts, and let a trigger keep each balance equal to the sum of its entries.

statement: Migrant workers' families cannot compare remittance charges across services.
topics: Hypothesis testing;Descriptive statistics;Charts and graphs
twist: Compare services with a two-sample test on fee percentages, so the app can say a difference is real and not noise.

statement: Commuters cannot tell which micro or bus route passes their stop in Kathmandu.
topics: Collections framework;Query processing and indexing;Cache and memory hierarchy;Swing GUI
twist: Routes are a graph built from plain Java collections, the stop index lets a lookup touch a handful of rows, and a small cache holds the most searched stops.

statement: Drivers cannot find which fuel station has petrol during a fuel shortage.
topics: Probability;Collections framework;Triggers
twist: Crowd reports can lie: weigh each report by the reporter's past accuracy with a simple Bayes update, and show the probability that a station really has fuel.

statement: Traffic police record violations on paper and fines are hard to verify later.
topics: Database security and access control;Backup and recovery;Triggers;Swing GUI
twist: A fine can never be quietly edited: append-only tables, role-based access, and a nightly backup with a restore that has actually been tested.

statement: Ward offices handle recommendation letters on paper and people make repeated visits.
topics: Process scheduling;Triggers;Stored procedures and functions
twist: Letters move through states like a process (new, ready, running, done) and the office queue uses round-robin, so no letter waits forever.

statement: Citizens do not know what documents are needed for common services and return several times.
topics: Swing GUI;File IO and serialization;Collections framework
twist: A touch-screen Swing kiosk that works from a local file with no network, with each checklist shown as a JTree from service down to documents.

statement: Social security allowance beneficiaries are not informed when payments are released.
topics: Multithreading;Semaphores and critical sections;Charts and graphs;Descriptive statistics
twist: Sending 10,000 SMS in one batch needs a worker pool: chart throughput as the thread count grows and show where more threads stop helping.

statement: Foreign-employment aspirants fall for fake manpower agencies charging illegal fees.
topics: Probability;Database security and access control;Triggers
twist: Each complaint raises an agency's risk score through a Bayes update, and every lookup is logged by a trigger so the board can show who searched what.

statement: Returnee migrant workers cannot show their skills to local employers.
topics: ER model and normalisation;Query processing and indexing;SQL views
twist: Skills are many-to-many: design the tables in 3NF, then show a join and a view that find returnees by any skill combination, and time it before and after an index.

statement: Daily wage workers gather at chowks waiting for work with no way to be booked in advance.
topics: Semaphores and critical sections;Locking and deadlock in databases;Transactions and ACID
twist: Many contractors may reach for the same worker in the same second: a semaphore-style row lock gives the worker to exactly one booking.

statement: Blood requests are spread through Facebook posts and many donors are contacted too late.
topics: Multithreading;Socket programming;Real-time systems
twist: A request fans out to nearby donors in parallel threads, the first acknowledgement stops the rest, and the response time is measured for every request.

statement: Community libraries and clubs cannot track volunteers' hours and skills.
solution: Volunteer Hours Log for Youth Clubs
topics: Descriptive statistics;Charts and graphs;SQL views
twist: Monthly hours as a histogram and a frequency polygon, with quartiles to show how evenly the club shares the work.

statement: Donated clothes and items pile up at one place while other shelters lack them.
topics: Deadlock and Banker's algorithm;Collections framework;Transactions and ACID
twist: Shelters request and donors supply: grant a request only if the system stays in a safe state, the Banker's algorithm applied to blankets and food packs.

statement: Local folk musicians have no place to publish and be discovered by listeners.
topics: File systems;Query processing and indexing;Page replacement;File IO and serialization
twist: Store the audio files in a directory scheme you design like a small file system, with an index for search and an LRU cache for the most played songs.

statement: Children learn traffic rules only from books and forget them quickly.
topics: Inheritance and polymorphism;Probability;Swing GUI
twist: Each sign is a class in a hierarchy, and the next question is picked by probability weighted toward the signs the child got wrong.

statement: Small cafes lose regular customers because they have no simple loyalty system.
topics: Database security and access control;Triggers;Descriptive statistics
twist: Each stamp is a QR token signed with a hash and a secret, so staff cannot fake it: encryption and non-repudiation from the security unit in a small, real setting.

statement: Local tailors lose customer measurements written in notebooks.
topics: Swing GUI;File IO and serialization;Backup and recovery
twist: A desktop order book that never loses a customer: every save writes a serialized snapshot and a database row, and restoring from the snapshot is part of the demo.
